recognize_zh: 中性球（上排）與單核球（下排）的細胞質都布滿粗大、深紫色的嗜天青顆粒，但沒有 Döhle 小體或空泡；顆粒同時出現在單核球，提示 Alder-Reilly 樣顆粒，符合黏多醣症第六型。
features: Segmented neutrophils (top) with cytoplasm packed with coarse, dark purple azurophilic granules
Monocytes (bottom) with folded or indented nuclei and blue-grey cytoplasm also studded with coarse purple granules
Granulation involves multiple lineages (neutrophils and monocytes), unlike toxic granulation
No Döhle bodies or cytoplasmic vacuoles in the neutrophils
A small lymphocyte (top right) lacks prominent granules; red cells unremarkable
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows segmented neutrophils and monocytes in which the cytoplasm is filled with coarse, dark azurophilic granules. The neutrophils lack accompanying Döhle bodies or vacuolation, and the monocytes are similarly granulated. An adjacent lymphocyte does not show conspicuous inclusions in this field. These Alder-Reilly-type granules, in the setting of low arylsulfatase B activity and urinary glycosaminoglycans, are consistent with mucopolysaccharidosis type VI (Maroteaux-Lamy syndrome).

ddx.vs: Toxic granulation affects neutrophils, usually with Döhle bodies, vacuoles and left shift, and does not involve monocytes.
G-CSF causes coarse granulation with Döhle bodies and left shift in neutrophils and resolves after therapy, in a clinical context of cytokine use.
Chediak-Higashi shows few giant fused granules rather than numerous uniform coarse granules, with albinism and immunodeficiency.
Morphology is similar (Alder-Reilly granules, lymphocyte inclusions); separation requires enzyme assay and gene testing (ARSB for MPS VI).
